title: Microbes in Human Welfare
syllabus: Microbes in household food processing; Microbes in industrial production (fermented beverages, antibiotics, chemicals, enzymes and other bioactive molecules); Microbes in sewage treatment (primary and secondary/biological treatment); Microbes in production of biogas (energy generation); Microbes as biocontrol agents; Microbes as biofertilizers.

questions.question: Lactic Acid Bacteria (LAB) convert milk into curd and improve its nutritional quality by significantly increasing the content of which vitamin?
questions.solution: During curd formation from milk, Lactic Acid Bacteria (LAB) produce acids that coagulate and partially digest milk proteins. LAB also improves the nutritional quality of curd by increasing the content of Vitamin B12.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the microbes utilized in household food processing:

List-I (Microbe)List-II (Product / Role)
(A) Saccharomyces cerevisiae(I) Large holes in Swiss cheese due to high production of $\text{CO}_2$
(B) Propionibacterium freudenreichii(II) Ripening of Roquefort cheese imparting a specific flavour
(C) Penicillium roqueforti(III) Fermentation of dough for bread making (Baker's yeast)
(D) Lactobacillus(IV) Conversion of milk into curd and checking disease-causing microbes in stomach

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Baker's yeast) ferments dough for bread; Propionibacterium freudenreichii (P. shermanii) produces large holes in Swiss cheese; Penicillium roqueforti ripens Roquefort cheese; Lactobacillus forms curd and checks pathogens in the gut.

questions.question: The puffed-up appearance of dough used for making dosa, idli, and bread is due to the production of which gas during fermentation?
questions.solution: The puffed-up appearance of fermented dough is caused by the release of carbon dioxide gas ($\text{CO}_2$) generated during anaerobic respiration (alcoholic fermentation) by yeasts and bacteria.

questions.question: 'Toddy', a traditional beverage of parts of southern India, is made by fermenting sap from:
questions.solution: 'Toddy' is a traditional drink of some parts of southern India prepared by fermenting the sugary sap collected from palm trees.

questions.question: Which of the following alcoholic beverages are produced by distillation of the fermented broth?
questions.solution: Wine and beer are produced without distillation (having lower alcohol concentrations), whereas whisky, brandy, and rum are produced by distillation of the fermented broth to yield higher alcohol percentages.

questions.question: Alexander Fleming discovered the first antibiotic, Penicillin, while working on which bacterium?
questions.solution: Alexander Fleming observed a mould, Penicillium notatum, growing on an unwashed culture plate of Staphylococcus bacteria, which prevented the bacteria from growing around it, leading to the discovery of penicillin.

questions.question: The full potential of Penicillin as an effective antibiotic was established during World War II by which scientists?
questions.solution: The full potential and commercial production of penicillin as an effective antibiotic was established by Ernest Chain and Howard Florey, who were awarded the Nobel Prize in 1945 along with Alexander Fleming.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the commercial production of organic acids by microbes:

List-I (Microorganism)List-II (Organic Acid Produced)
(A) Aspergillus niger (Fungus)(I) Butyric acid
(B) Acetobacter aceti (Bacterium)(II) Lactic acid
(C) Clostridium butylicum (Bacterium)(III) Citric acid
(D) Lactobacillus (Bacterium)(IV) Acetic acid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Aspergillus niger: Citric acid; Acetobacter aceti: Acetic acid; Clostridium butylicum: Butyric acid; Lactobacillus: Lactic acid.

questions.question: Which of the following enzymes is used in detergent formulations to help remove oily stains from laundry?
questions.solution: Lipases (produced by microbes like Candida) are utilized in detergent formulations and are helpful in removing oily and greasy stains from laundry fabrics.

questions.question: Bottled fruit juices bought from the market are clearer compared to those made at home because commercial juices are clarified using:
questions.solution: Commercial bottled fruit juices are clarified by treatment with the enzymes pectinases and proteases, which digest insoluble fruit pulp pectins and proteins.

questions.question: Streptokinase, an enzyme produced by the bacterium Streptococcus and modified by genetic engineering, is used clinically as a:
options: 'Clot buster' for removing thrombi from blood vessels of myocardial infarction patients
questions.solution: Streptokinase produced by Streptococcus (modified by genetic engineering) is used as a 'clot buster' to dissolve intravascular blood clots in patients who have suffered myocardial infarction leading to heart attack.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding bioactive molecules, their microbial sources, and clinical applications:

List-I (Bioactive Molecule)List-II (Source & Medical Application)
(A) Cyclosporin A(I) Monascus purpureus; Blood cholesterol-lowering statin (inhibits HMG-CoA reductase)
(B) Statins(II) Trichoderma polysporum; Immunosuppressive agent in organ transplant patients
(C) Streptokinase(III) Streptococcus; Clot buster for dissolving intravascular thrombi

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Cyclosporin A (from the fungus Trichoderma polysporum) is an immunosuppressive drug used in organ transplant patients; Statins (from the yeast Monascus purpureus) act as competitive inhibitors of the enzyme responsible for cholesterol synthesis; Streptokinase is a clot buster.

questions.question: Statins lower blood cholesterol levels by acting as competitive inhibitors of the enzyme responsible for synthesizing cholesterol. Statins are commercially produced from the yeast:
questions.solution: Statins produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus have been commercialized as blood cholesterol-lowering agents. They function by competitively inhibiting the enzyme HMG-CoA reductase involved in cholesterol synthesis.

questions.question: In sewage treatment plants (STPs), the primary physical treatment step involves:
options: Sequential filtration and sedimentation to remove floating debris and grit (soil and small pebbles)
Aerobic digestion using bacterial and fungal flocs
Anaerobic digestion of organic matter in sludge digesters
Chlorination and UV disinfection of clean effluent
questions.solution: Primary treatment is a physical process that removes large and small particles from sewage through sequential filtration (removing floating debris) and sedimentation (settling of grit, soil, and small pebbles in settling tanks).

questions.question: What happens to the Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) of sewage wastewater as it undergoes effective secondary (biological) treatment?
options: BOD decreases significantly as organic matter is consumed by aerobic microbial flocs
BOD drops to zero instantly in the primary settling tank
questions.solution: BOD measures the amount of oxygen required by microorganisms to oxidize the organic matter in one litre of water. As aerobic microbes in aeration tanks consume organic pollutants, the BOD decreases significantly. A lower BOD indicates cleaner water.

questions.question: In the aeration tanks of secondary sewage treatment, the vigorous growth of useful aerobic microbes forms 'flocs'. Flocs are defined as:
options: Masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments to form mesh-like structures
Insoluble deposits of sand and gravel
Floating scum of oils and fats
questions.solution: Flocs are masses of aerobic bacteria associated with fungal hyphae to form mesh-like structures that rapidly digest organic matter in aeration tanks.

questions.question: During secondary sewage treatment, when the BOD of wastewater is reduced significantly, the effluent is passed into a settling tank where bacterial flocs are allowed to sediment. This sediment is called:
questions.solution: Once the BOD of sewage is reduced, the effluent passes into a settling tank where the microbial flocs settle under gravity. This sediment is called activated sludge.

questions.question: A small part of the activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as an ________, while the remaining major part is pumped into ________:
questions.solution: A small fraction of activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as an inoculum (starter culture), while the remaining major portion is pumped into large anaerobic sludge digesters.

questions.question: In anaerobic sludge digesters, anaerobic bacteria digest the bacteria and fungi present in the sludge, producing a mixture of biogas containing:
options: Methane ($\text{CH}_4$), Hydrogen sulphide ($\text{H}_2\text{S}$), and Carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$)
Carbon dioxide, Sulfur dioxide, and Oxygen
questions.solution: In anaerobic sludge digesters, anaerobic bacteria digest the organic matter, producing biogas—a mixture of gases consisting primarily of methane ($\text{CH}_4$, $50-70\%$), carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$, $30-40\%$), and traces of hydrogen sulphide ($\text{H}_2\text{S}$).

questions.question: The Ministry of Environment and Forests initiated the Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan in India primarily to:
options: Build a large number of Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) so that only treated sewage is discharged into rivers
Ban fishing and navigation in rivers
Promote chemical fertilizer discharge into rivers
Divert river water completely for thermal power stations
questions.solution: Under the Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan, the government envisioned the construction of numerous modern STPs so that only biologically treated, non-polluting water is discharged into major rivers.

questions.question: Methanogens (e.g., Methanobacterium) are obligate anaerobic archaebacteria that grow on cellulosic material to produce biogas. They are found in:
options: Anaerobic sludge digesters and the rumen (first stomach chamber) of cattle
Upper soil horizons in presence of high oxygen
questions.solution: Methanogens commonly thrive in the anaerobic sludge during sewage treatment, in marshy lands, and in the rumen of cattle, where they assist in the breakdown of dietary cellulose.

questions.question: The technology of biogas production from animal dung (Gobar gas) was developed in India largely due to the pioneering collaborative efforts of:
options: Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) and Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)
Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and CSIR
Ministry of Environment and Forests (MoEF) and WHO
questions.solution: The technology of rural biogas production was developed in India largely through the research and extension efforts of the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) and the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding biological control agents (Biocontrol) and their target agricultural pests:

List-I (Biocontrol Agent)List-II (Target Pest Controlled)
(A) Ladybird beetle (with red & black markings)(I) Mosquito larvae
(B) Dragonflies(II) Aphids
(C) Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt)(III) Plant fungal pathogens in the root ecosystem
(D) Trichoderma (free-living fungus)(IV) Butterfly caterpillars and insect larvae

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Ladybird beetles control aphids; Dragonflies eliminate mosquitoes; Bacillus thuringiensis controls butterfly caterpillars and insect pests; Trichoderma is a soil fungus that protects roots from fungal pathogens.

questions.question: Baculoviruses used as biological control agents belong to the genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus. They are considered ideal biocontrol candidates because they are:
options: Species-specific, narrow-spectrum insecticides with no negative impact on plants, mammals, birds, fish, or non-target insects
Pathogenic to beneficial honeybees and earthworms
questions.solution: Baculoviruses (genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus) are excellent pathogens for narrow-spectrum, species-specific insecticidal applications. They have no negative impacts on plants, mammals, birds, fish, or non-target insects, making them ideal for Integrated Pest Management (IPM) in ecologically sensitive areas.

questions.question: A free-living soil fungus that is very common in root ecosystems and acts as an effective biocontrol agent against several plant pathogens is:
questions.solution: Trichoderma species are free-living fungi that are very common in root ecosystems. They are effective biocontrol agents against several soil-borne plant pathogens.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding Nitrogen-fixing biofertilizers and their associations:

List-I (Biofertilizer)List-II (Nature of Association / Organism)
(A) Rhizobium(I) Free-living anaerobic nitrogen-fixing bacterium in soil
(B) Azotobacter and Azospirillum(II) Symbiotic association inside root nodules of leguminous plants
(C) Clostridium(III) Free-living aerobic nitrogen-fixing bacteria in soil
(D) Anabaena azollae(IV) Symbiotic cyanobacterium in the aquatic fern Azolla (used in paddy fields)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Rhizobium: Symbiotic in legume root nodules; Azotobacter / Azospirillum: Free-living aerobic $\text{N}_2$ fixers; Clostridium: Free-living anaerobic $\text{N}_2$ fixer; Anabaena azollae: Symbiont in Azolla fronds, used extensively as biofertilizer in paddy (rice) fields.

questions.question: Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association between a fungus and roots of higher plants (e.g., genus Glomus). The fungal symbiont provides which major benefit to the host plant?
options: Absorbs phosphorus from soil and passes it to the plant, and provides resistance to root-borne pathogens and salinity/drought
Fixes atmospheric nitrogen into nitrates directly
questions.solution: Fungi of the genus Glomus form mycorrhizal associations. The fungal hyphae absorb phosphorus from the soil and pass it to the host plant, while conferring resistance to root-borne pathogens, tolerance to salinity and drought, and overall improvement in plant growth.

questions.question: Which of the following cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) serve as important biofertilizers in paddy (rice) fields by fixing atmospheric nitrogen and adding organic matter to the soil?
questions.solution: Cyanobacteria such as Anabaena, Nostoc, and Oscillatoria are autotrophic microbes that fix atmospheric nitrogen and enrich soil fertility, serving as important biofertilizers, particularly in paddy fields.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the role of microbes in sewage treatment:
Statement I: Secondary treatment of sewage is fundamentally a biological process that utilizes aerobic and anaerobic microbes.
Statement II: The greater the BOD of wastewater, the lesser is its polluting potential.

Choose the correct option:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Statement I is correct because secondary sewage treatment is biological. Statement II is incorrect because a higher BOD indicates a greater amount of organic matter present in the water, signifying higher polluting potential.

questions.question: Dried spores of Bacillus thuringiensis are mixed with water and sprayed onto vulnerable plants like brassicas and fruit trees. When eaten by insect larvae, the toxin is activated in the:
options: Alkaline pH of the insect midgut, creating pores that cause cell swelling and lysis
Acidic pH of the insect foregut
questions.solution: The inactive protoxin of Bt is ingested by insect larvae and becomes solubilized and active in the alkaline pH of the insect midgut. The active toxin binds to midgut epithelial cells, creating pores that cause cell swelling and lysis, leading to death.

questions.question: Which of the following organic acids is produced by the microbial fermentation of the bacterium Acetobacter aceti?
questions.solution: Acetobacter aceti is an obligate aerobic bacterium that oxidizes ethanol into acetic acid (vinegar).

questions.question: A typical rural biogas plant consists of a concrete tank ($10 - 15\text{ feet}$ deep) in which bio-wastes and a slurry of dung are fed. The floating cover placed over the slurry:
options: Keeps on rising as the biogas is produced in the tank due to microbial activity
Permits continuous aeration of the slurry
Filters the solid sludge directly into the fields
Heats the dung using solar radiation
questions.solution: A floating gas holder (cover) placed over the digester slurry rises as biogas is produced by anaerobic methanogens, creating pressure to supply gas through an outlet pipe to nearby households.

questions.question: Which of the following microbes is used for the commercial ripening and flavour enhancement of Swiss cheese?
questions.solution: The large holes in Swiss cheese are produced by the bacterium Propionibacterium freudenreichii (P. shermanii) due to the production of a large volume of $\text{CO}_2$ along with propionic acid.

questions.question: Chemical pesticides and insecticides indiscriminately kill both useful and harmful organisms. Integrated Pest Management (IPM) using biocontrol methods aims to:
options: Manage pests at manageable levels through natural predation and holistic ecosystem balance without eradicating all species
Completely eradicate every insect species from agricultural fields
Replace all crops with chemical synthetic polymers
questions.solution: Biocontrol in organic farming aims to manage pests at sustainable ecological levels using natural predators rather than completely eradicating them, which would also starve beneficial predatory and parasitic insects.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is a free-living, aerobic nitrogen-fixing bacterium in soil?
questions.solution: Azotobacter and Azospirillum are free-living, aerobic nitrogen-fixing soil bacteria that enrich the nitrogen content of the soil without forming symbiotic root nodules.

questions.question: Cyclosporin A, an immunosuppressive drug that prevents graft rejection in kidney and heart transplant patients, is extracted from the fungus:
questions.solution: Cyclosporin A is a cyclic non-ribosomal peptide produced by the soil fungus Trichoderma polysporum and is widely used as an immunosuppressant in organ transplant recipients.

questions.question:
Read the following statements:
Statement I: Primary sludge requires no aeration and is directly composed of settleable solids removed during physical sedimentation.
Statement II: Treatment of sewage wastewater is carried out until the BOD is reduced significantly.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Primary sludge consists of settled solid particles from primary physical treatment; secondary biological treatment continues in aeration basins until the BOD is reduced to acceptable standards.

questions.question: The spent slurry left behind in a biogas plant after gas extraction is widely used as:
options: An excellent manure/fertilizer rich in nitrogen and phosphorus for agricultural fields
An artificial substrate for tissue culture
questions.solution: The spent digested slurry is removed through an outlet pipe and used as rich organic manure for crops because it retains nitrogen, phosphorus, and essential minerals.

questions.question: Which of the following is an aquatic fern that harbors the nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium Anabaena in its leaf cavities and serves as an excellent biofertilizer in rice paddy fields?
questions.solution: Azolla pinnata is a small free-floating aquatic fern that maintains a symbiotic association with the cyanobacterium Anabaena azollae, significantly boosting rice yields when used as a green manure biofertilizer.

questions.question: Frankia is a nitrogen-fixing actinomycete (microbe) that forms root nodules symbiotically in:
options: Leguminous plants like Pea and Gram
Monocot cereal grasses like Rice and Wheat
questions.solution: Frankia is a filamentous nitrogen-fixing microbe that forms symbiotic nitrogen-fixing root nodules in non-leguminous plants such as Alnus and Casuarina. Rhizobium nodulates legumes.

questions.question: Brewer's yeast, used for fermenting malted cereals and fruit juices to produce ethanol, belongs to the species:
questions.solution: Saccharomyces cerevisiae, commonly known as Brewer's yeast (and Baker's yeast), is used for fermenting malted cereals and fruit juices into ethanol and $\text{CO}_2$.

questions.question: During secondary treatment of sewage, what is the main purpose of constantly pumping air into large aeration tanks?
options: To allow vigorous growth of useful aerobic heterotrophic microbes into flocs
To kill all microorganisms through aerobic shock
questions.solution: Air is pumped vigorously into aeration tanks to provide oxygen for the rapid growth of aerobic heterotrophic microorganisms into flocs, which consume the dissolved organic matter.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-symbiotic (free-living) anaerobic bacterium capable of fixing atmospheric nitrogen in soil?
questions.solution: Clostridium is a free-living, anaerobic nitrogen-fixing bacterium found in soil. Azotobacter is aerobic, while Rhizobium and Frankia are symbiotic.

questions.question: Biofertilizers are defined as organisms that:
options: Enrich the nutrient quality of the soil through biological processes like nitrogen fixation, phosphorus solubilization, and organic matter synthesis
Eradicate soil insect pests using chemical toxins
Prevent all transpiration water loss from plant roots
Produce petrochemical fuels directly from soil
questions.solution: Biofertilizers are living microorganisms (bacteria, fungi, and cyanobacteria) that enrich the nutrient quality of the soil by fixing atmospheric nitrogen, solubilizing phosphorus, or forming symbiotic nutrient-absorbing networks.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding Baculoviruses:
Statement I: Baculoviruses are pathogens that attack insects and other arthropods.
Statement II: They have broad-spectrum activity and kill all beneficial non-target pollinator insects.

Choose the correct option:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Statement I is correct because baculoviruses attack arthropods. Statement II is incorrect because baculoviruses are species-specific, narrow-spectrum biocontrol agents that do not harm non-target or pollinating insects.
